author: Rory Robinson
title: North Carolina 'under investigation' amid Michael Lombardi bombshell - NewsBreak
text:
By Rory Robinson ,
2 days ago North Carolina hired Bill Belichick to make the Tar Heels more competitive in the ACC, and Belichick hired Michael Lombardi as his first General Manager to ensure the program is equipped to see out this Super Bowl-winning coach's vision.
The Tar Heels won only four games last season, Lombardi is now sidelined after an alleged HR complaint , and the entire school is now reportedly under investigation over potential foul play regarding NCAA and NIL rules.
According to investigative journalist Pablo Torre, the UNC college football program is being investigated by the College Sports Commission. It's unclear if the probe is tied to Lobmardi's situation in any way. The CSC oversees Division I compliance tied to NIL valuations, roster caps, and institutional revenue sharing.
Meanwhile, Belichick's girlfriend is threatening to sue investigative journalists for probing into their relationship.
• UNC 'investigating HR complaint' made against Michael Lombardi before paid leave
• UNC's strict instructions to players and staff over Michael Lombardi suspension
If the CSC finds violations of structural rules or inflated third-party contracts, the Tar Heels could face major athletic department fines of up to 20 percent of the football budget and restrictions on future NIL distributions.
The independent regulatory company earned its first college sports victory after a judge ruled in May to block $7.5 million in contracts for 18 Nebraska football players for violating spending rules.
North Carolina football reportedly upgraded its NIL budget from $4 million to $20 million last season. Redshirt junior quarterback Gio Lopez signed a two-year, $4 million contract with UNC after a 2025 transfer portal move from South Alabama.
Lombardi was placed on paid administrative leave on Monday after a former front-office employee reportedly filed a formal HR complaint.
The GM worked closely alongside coach Belichick and was the former New England Patriots coach's first hire in December 2024. He held his role for roughly one year and seven months before being placed on leave.
The university confirmed that athletic department staff, leadership, and players are prohibited from discussing the active personnel matter, according to Vice Chancellor for Communications and Marketing Dean Stoyer.
Belichick's first season ended 4-8 overall and 2-6 in the ACC, and UNC responded by overhauling the roster with Lombardi's help. The school brought in more than 60 new players for 2026 and secured a recruiting class ranked No. 12 by ESPN.
UNC's 2026 class includes quarterback Travis Burgess, running back Crew Davis, receivers Carnell Warren, Nyqir Helton, Zamaurious Robertson, and Kymistrii Young, plus major trench additions across the offensive and defensive lines.
The grueling college football schedule will also not wait for UNC to clean up its compliance mess. The Tar Heels open against TCU in Dublin, then face Clemson, Notre Dame, Duke, Miami, Louisville and NC State.
